about: Principal Skinner is a two-panel shot from The Simpsons. In the top panel Seymour Skinner stands outside with his chin in his hand, brow furrowed, honestly asking himself whether he is out of touch. In the bottom panel his face relaxes into calm, wide-eyed certainty as he concludes that no, it is the children who are wrong. The meme captures someone who briefly considers being wrong and then talks themselves straight back out of it, and it is used to tease stubborn people, companies, critics and anyone who blames everyone else.
origin: The scene is from The Simpsons season 5 episode "The Boy Who Knew Too Much," first aired in May 1994. Skinner's moment of doubt and instant self-acquittal became one of the show's most quoted lines.
usage:
The first box sits under the thoughtful top panel and holds the brief moment of self-reflection: "am I so out of touch?" or a question about whether you are the problem. The second box under the calm panel holds the self-serving conclusion that everyone else is wrong.

It works for any person or institution doubling down: a studio blaming players for low sales, a manager blaming staff, you blaming the recipe. The best captions make the first panel sound reasonable so the second feels even more delusional.
